Aiyoo, another spring already. Let me think about this year on my 10.9 mu. My wife and I, we've been doing this same way for many years — the kids went off to the city so it's just the two of us now at 50. I never went to school, but I've been on this land 30 years. I know what the ground tells me.

**The wheat (8 mu).** Already in the ground since October, like always. Came up fine before winter. Now in April it's getting tall, greening up. I already put down one bag of that compound fertilizer per mu before planting last fall — that's the 15-15-15, one 50 kg bag per mu, same as Old Chen down the road does. Now I need to topdress. When I see the wheat at jointing, maybe end of April or early May, I'll scatter about half a bag of urea per mu — maybe a little more if it looks yellow. Then I irrigate. This year I'll probably water three times — once at jointing, once at heading, once when the grain is filling. The well is working fine, but pumping costs money. If it rains good, I'll skip one. Harvest in June, like always. If Heaven gives us good weather, maybe 400 kg per mu. My neighbor got more last year but he puts down two bags of compound — I can't afford that every year.

**The maize (8 mu, right after wheat).** Very tight. Between cutting the wheat and putting in the maize, maybe only three or four days. I buy the hybrid seed from the shop in the village — the red bag one, the shopkeeper tells me which is good. Plant mid-June. I'll put about one bag of compound per mu at planting, and later when the maize is knee-high I topdress some urea, maybe 20 kg per mu. Usually I water once or twice in July-August if it's dry. Maize does OK without much water here if the rain comes. If it's a dry year, different story. Harvest late September. Hoping for 450 kg per mu.

**The vegetables — eggplant (1 mu), tomato (1 mu), watermelon (0.9 mu).** These bring in cash. But they're a lot of work for two old people. I keep them small for that reason. My wife takes care of the vegetables mostly, I do the grain. I bought the seedlings from the market last week for the eggplant and tomato — transplanting them now in late April, they go under small plastic covers for the cold nights. Watermelon I direct-seed on little mounds, same time. 

For vegetables I put on more fertilizer — vegetables are hungry. For eggplant and tomato, I mix in chicken manure I got cheap from the chicken farmer, plus about two bags of compound per mu, and I top up with urea every few weeks when I see they need it. Watermelon I don't push too hard on nitrogen or the fruit won't be sweet — more potash, one bag of compound plus some of that potassium fertilizer. 

I irrigate vegetables often, every week or so when it's dry, through a little hose from the well. Pesticide — yes, I have to spray. Eggplant gets those little bugs, tomato gets the worms. I buy what the shopkeeper recommends, spray maybe four or five times over the season. Same for the watermelon.

Yields — eggplant and tomato I can get maybe 3000-3500 kg per mu if the weather is OK and the market is good. Watermelon maybe 2000-2500 kg. Prices go up and down. Last year tomato was cheap, lost money almost. But we keep going.

**Money.** Biggest worry. Fertilizer went up again this year, one bag costs more than last year. I have to be careful. I don't take credit if I can help it — my father said never borrow to farm.

**Labor.** Just me and my wife. We can manage the wheat and maize ourselves. For vegetables, if picking gets too much in July I might pay my cousin's boy for a few days, 100 yuan a day. Otherwise we do it all.

**Tradeoffs.** If I put more fertilizer on wheat, maybe higher yield but less cash for the maize seed and vegetable seedlings. If I skip an irrigation on wheat to save money, risk losing yield if May is dry. I choose the middle — not cheap, not extravagant. Same as always.
